input.prompt: First-person view of a plague doctor who has just stepped into a poor peasant hut in a remote rural village, at night, in an undefined, timeless era: no electricity and no modern objects. The single room has walls of rough stone and cracked clay, a low ceiling of soot-blackened beams, a beaten-earth floor with scattered straw, a smoky hearth with glowing embers on the left, a crude wooden table with a tallow candle, a clay jug, a loaf of dark bread and four wooden bowls, a ladder climbing to a dark loft, and at the back a ragged curtain half hiding a sleeping alcove. A poor family stands facing the doctor in tense silence: a gaunt father in a patched wool coat with a forced, tight-lipped smile; a frightened mother in a headscarf clutching her shawl; a thin girl half hidden behind her. Their faces are weathered, unidealized and subtly unsettling; they are hiding someone. In the lower right foreground, the doctor's own black leather glove holds a long wooden cane, like the held item in a first-person video game. Realistic photograph, evenly lit by the candle and the hearth so that every face and object is clearly readable. 16:9, no text, no border.
